outcome: incidence of invasive procedures (conservative surgery, embolisation, hysterectomy)
transfer to centers with arterial embolisation facilities
cohort: 109 patients with postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) refractory to sulprostone from a tertiary care center, separated into two groups: before (2008–2010) and after (2015–2017) the introduction of an intrauterine tamponade balloon protocol.
finding: The introduction of intrauterine tamponade was associated with a decrease in the need for invasive procedures and transfer rates for PPH management.
